note: Satire of real stories from the week of 2026-11-16. Parody names only; nobody real is named.

arrivals: {city} port's cargo cranes start moving on their own after a 'routine update'
Payment terminals across {city} reboot at once. Coffee is free for nine minutes.
early: Hackers slip wallet-swapping code into 178 big websites through one shared plugin. The plugin was 'very popular'.
Security firm reports the first hack with no human involved at any step. Police unsure who to arrest.
Police seize 235 criminal servers in a single morning. A 236th sends a thank-you note.
Furniture chain leaks 37 million customer records. The assembly instructions remain a secret.
Remote-support company's own support accounts hacked. A support ticket has been opened.
New rules close the 'just rent the chips abroad' loophole. Data center landlords in shock.
Southeast Asia's data center boom now needs a license for every chip. Paper shredders sell out.
City library hit by ransomware. Late fees forgiven 'for now'.
middle: Drone maker hacked. Investigators still checking whether the drones noticed.
University systems offline for a week. Students call it 'the best week of the semester'.
Patch released 9 minutes after a bug is found. The exploit came out 4 minutes before that.

Security researchers find malware that writes its own patch notes
late: Last human ransomware gang retires, citing 'unfair competition'
hopeful: Police take down a botnet in one morning. For once, it doesn't come back.
